title: Sloped glass.
officialText:
Glass sloped more than 15 degrees (0.26 rad) from vertical in skylights, sunrooms, sloped roofs and other exterior applications shall be designed to resist the most critical of the following combinations of loads. F = W – D (Equation 24-2) g o F = Wi+ D + 0.5S (Equation 24-3) g F =0.5 Wi+D+S (Equation 24-4) g where: D = Glass dead load (kN/m2). For glass sloped 30 degrees (0.52 rad) or less from horizontal,

= 13 t (For SI: 0.0245 t ) g g For glass sloped more than 30 degrees (0.52 rad) from horizontal,

= 13 t cos θ (For SI: 0.0245 t cos θ). g g F = Total load, psf (kN/m2) on glass. g S = Snow load, psf (kN/m2) as determined in Section 1608.

t = Total glass thickness, inches (mm) of glass panes and plies. g W = Inward wind force, psf (kN/m2) as calculated in Section 1609. i W = Outward wind force, psf (kN/m2) as calculated in Section 1609. o

θ = Angle of slope from horizontal.
Exception: Unit skylights shall be designed in accordance with Section 2405.5.

The design of sloped glazing shall be based on the following equation: F < F (Equation 24-5) g ga where: F = Total load on the glass determined from the load combinations above. g F = Short duration load resistance of the glass as determined according to ASTM E 1300 for Equations 24-2 and 24-3; or the long duration ga load resistance of the glass as determined according to ASTM E 1300 for Equation 24-4.
